Sharma, Panel Lawyer Sb: Hon'ble Shri Parth Prateem Sahu, Judge Order

This is the second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail, as he has been arrested in connection with Crime No. 320/2023 registered at Police Station - Ganj, District - Raipur, Chhattisgarh for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 376 (2) (n), 506, 509 (B) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

entities.text: Police Station - Ganj, District - Raipur, Chhattisgarh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
2. Case of prosecution is that, the applicant sent several messages to victim on 'Instagram'
whereupon victim made a call to applicant. After sometime, applicant told that he can arrange job for her on giving him Rs. 60,000/- to which, victim agreed.

Thereafter, applicant came to Raipur,
contacted the victim over mobile phone and asked her to come to hotel to give the money.
Victim went to the hotel and handed over the money to applicant.
However, in the hotel, applicant forcibly established physical relation with victim and also prepared video recording and photographs of their relationship.

Thereafter, applicant under the threat of making viral obscene photographs and video clips of victim, committed sexual intercourse with her on many occasions and also taken money from her, total amounting to Rs. 2 Lakhs.
When victim refused to satisfy illegal demands of applicant and asked him to return her money, he forwarded obscene photographs and video clips to the mobile phones of her in- laws.

Thereafter, report was lodged in concerned police station based upon which aforementioned crime was registered and the applicant was arrested on 30.10.2023 Akhilesh Yadav @ Rahul vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72937294/
1 3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that after rejection of the first bail application, victim has now been examined and therefore, there is no likelihood of influencing the material witnesses.

Victim was examined on 04.07.2024, there are as many as 20 witnesses, trial may take sometime,
age of the victim is 34 years.
Hence, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

4. On the other hand, learned State counsel opposes the submission made by learned counsel for the applicant and would submit that there are specific allegation of commission of forceful sexual intercourse with the victim and also blackmailing her by showing the obscene photographs clicked by the applicant.
However, he do not dispute the age of the victim to be 34 years on the date of incident.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the respective parties.

6. Taking into consideration, facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegations, submission of learned counsel for the respective parties, period of detention, victim is examined before the learned Trial Court, trial may take sometime, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, I am inclined to allow this application for grant of bail.
7.

Accordingly, the bail application filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is allowed and it is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to satisfaction of Trial Court concerned on the conditions that:
(i) He shall appear before the Trial Court concerned regularly on each and every date unless exempted from appearance.
(ii)He shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
(iii) If applicant is found involved in similar offence in future, it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of bail.
Certified copy as per rules.

Sd/-
(Parth Prateem Sahu) Judge Dey Akhilesh Yadav @ Rahul vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72937294/
